 Browns vs. Saints odds, picks, prediction, spread: Start time, NFL Week 9 betting preview, best bets
 Here's everything bettors need to know for Browns vs. Saints in NFL Week 9
 By
 Brandon Gustafson 
 Nov 8, 2026
 at
 7:35 am ET 
 •
 2 min read
 The New Orleans Saints (2-5) host the Cleveland Browns (5-3) in Week 9. New Orleans has won just one of its last five games but could have an opportunity for a positive result on Sunday with Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson out due to a concussion. We're looking at the latest Saints vs. Browns odds at DraftKings Sportsbook  and highlighting our NFL best bets. The model entered Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season on a 60-51 run on top-rated picks dating back to 2024. Anybody following its picks at  NFL betting sites  could have seen strong returns.  
 Browns vs. Saints betting odds (via DraftKings)
 Browns vs. Saints money line: Saints -162, Browns +136 
 Browns vs. Saints   Over/Under: 42.5 (Over -110, Under -110) 
 Browns vs. Saints spread:  Saints -3 
 Browns vs. Saints betting preview
 Saints fans have not had much to celebrate this season. Second-year quarterback Tyler Shough has shown himself to be a capable signal caller, but there hasn't been enough around him on either side of the ball. The New Orleans defense has given up 27.7 points per game, the fourth most in the league, putting serious pressure on an offense that's been middling at best. 
 And while Cleveland may have a winning record, all signs point to imminent regression. Three of the Browns' wins have come over half-baked teams -- Tampa Bay, Tennessee and a Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore. The defense has been merely fine and the offense has managed just 17.4 points per game. That offense will now be in the hands of backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders with Watson sidelined.
 This game may not be one for the purists.

 Saints money line
 This line didn't move much when news emerged that Watson was unlikely to play on Sunday, an indication that the oddsmakers were already anticipating as much. The veteran hasn't exactly been impressive this season, which shows just how eager the Browns really are to throw Sanders into the fire.
